title: Key-Dependent Correlation in ChaCha Bit Puncturing
summary: Existing ChaCha bit-puncturing analysis estimates only average correlation; determine its variation across keys and derive reliable key-dependent attack success probabilities.

formal_statement.body: For ChaCha bit-puncturing attacks, determine how the correlation induced by the punctured key bits varies with the secret key and derive a key-dependent success-probability analysis. The available analysis estimates only the average correlation over punctured key bits, while experiments show that the right-key distribution has higher variance than expected; this discrepancy is believed to result from absorbing the secret key with modular addition rather than XOR. The unresolved task is to establish reliable variance bounds or key-distribution quantiles and use them to quantify attack success probability across keys, rather than relying on the average correlation.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of ChaCha bit-puncturing attacks, focusing on correlation statistics and attack success across keys.
parameters: Secret key — conditions the correlation and attack success probability
Punctured key bits — induce the correlation for which the current analysis estimates only an average
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize correlation across secret keys, establish reliable variance bounds or key-distribution quantiles, and use them to quantify attack success probability across keys.

progress.summary: The source reports greater-than-expected experimental variance in the right-key distribution and suggests modular key addition as the cause. Its calculations estimate only average correlation, leaving key-dependent success analysis unresolved.
